statement: Calef states that Captain Hall's battery of the First Corps (printed Rhode Island, bracketed Maine in the print) took the first position on the right of the road held by Lieutenant Roder's section after that section had withdrawn, that in about half an hour the battery was disabled and withdrew leaving two pieces on the field.

source.author: Lieut. John H. Calef
source.quote: Captain Hall's (Rhode Island) [Maine] battery, belonging to the First Corps,
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R374 Lieut. John H. Calef, p. 1031

The left and center sections of Calef's battery were ordered up again by General Wadsworth to reoccupy the ground Hall abandoned.

statement: Osborn states that on the afternoon of 1 July Colonel Wainwright, chief of artillery of the First Corps, took command of Captain Wiedrich's battery, in front of the cemetery entrance, with the artillery on that side of the Baltimore pike, and that Osborn furnished Wainwright with ammunition from the Eleventh Corps train during that afternoon and the morning of the 2d.
reasoning: Osborn prints that Wiedrich's battery stood on the hill immediately in front of the cemetery entrance; on that afternoon Wainwright took command of it with the artillery on that side of the Baltimore pike, which Hunt (R028) and Wainwright (R071) put outside the cemetery gate north of the pike (East Cemetery Hill).

statement: Ricketts states that at 4 p. m. on 2 July Captain Huntington ordered him to report to Colonel C. S. Wainwright, First New York Artillery, who placed him in position on Cemetery Hill to the right of the turnpike leading into Gettysburg.
reasoning: The turnpike leading into Gettysburg is the Baltimore pike; the ground to its right facing the town is East Cemetery Hill (the hill Ricketts' battery held, PA2-S035), where Wainwright's batteries stood outside the cemetery gate.

source.author: Capt. R. Bruce Ricketts
source.quote: who placed me in position on Cemetery Hill, to the right of the turnpike
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R328 Capt. R. Bruce Ricketts, p. 894

place.printed: Cemetery Hill, to the right of the turnpike leading into Gettysburg

statement: Norton, commanding Battery H, 1st Ohio Light Artillery, states that on the morning after the battle of Friday (4 July) his battery was sent up to relieve one of the batteries of the First Corps, by request of Colonel Wainwright, and occupied gun-covers near the cemetery until the afternoon of the 5th.
reasoning: Norton prints that after the battle of Friday (3 July) his battery went to the rear and the next morning (4 July) was sent up to relieve one of the batteries of the First Corps by request of Colonel Wainwright, chief of artillery; he does not name the battery, so the record is the artillery brigade's.

source.author: Lieut. George W. Norton
source.quote: relieve one of the batteries of the First Corps, by request of Colonel Wainwright,
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R327 Lieut. George W. Norton, p. 894

place.printed: gun-covers near the cemetery

note: The battery relieved is not named; the date follows the report: after the close of the battle of Friday, the next morning is Saturday, 4 July.

statement: Doubleday states that on 30 June the First Corps made a short march of 3 or 4 miles to Marsh Creek, where it again took up a defensive position, Wadsworth's division, with Hall's Second Maine Battery, covering the Gettysburg road.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: we made a short march of 3 or 4 miles to Marsh Creek,
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 243

place.printed: Marsh Creek

Morrow (R033) prints that the Twenty-fourth Michigan bivouacked near Marsh Creek on 30 June, Wister (R062) puts the Third Division on the north side of Marsh Creek about 6 miles from Gettysburg, and the itinerary (R007) prints Marsh Run for the corps: the stage is one.

statement: Doubleday states that on 30 June at Marsh Creek Wadsworth's division, with Hall's Second Maine Battery, covered the Gettysburg road.

source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 244

source.author: Col. Charles S. Wainwright
source.quote: was in position a couple of miles farther on, commanding the bridge

statement: Hall states that his battery was in camp on the morning of 1 July at Marsh Creek, 4 miles from Gettysburg.

source.author: Capt. James A. Hall

statement: Hall states that at 9 a. m. on 1 July his battery marched from Marsh Creek, following the advance brigade of the First Division, First Army Corps, to the battlefield, about half a mile south and west of the town.

statement: Doubleday states that between 7 and 8 o'clock on the morning of 1 July General Reynolds, sending for him, told him that he had already given orders to Wadsworth's division, with Hall's battery, to move forward and that he would accompany those troops in person.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: had already given orders to Wadsworth's division, with Hall's battery, to move forward,

statement: Doubleday states that when he overtook Wadsworth's division it had left the main road and was filing rapidly through woods and fields toward a ridge running north and south about 400 yards west of the seminary.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: had left the main road and was filing rapidly through woods and fields
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 244

when.printed: I pushed forward at full speed

note: Wadsworth (R032) prints that the division struck the Cashtown road three-quarters of a mile west of Gettysburg at about 10 a. m. after leaving the column's line of march across the fields; the report does not name the main road: it is the road from Emmitsburg, the road of the approach of every other record.

statement: Doubleday states that, owing to the intervals between the divisions and the need of calling in the pickets, an hour and a half to two hours elapsed before the remaining troops of the corps were en route, so that Wadsworth's division was obliged to sustain the brunt of the action alone for this length of time.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday

statement: Doubleday states that on the most westerly of the ridges west of the seminary General Reynolds had directed his line of battle to be formed and was himself superintending the placing of Cutler's brigade as Doubleday rode up.
reasoning: Doubleday prints that on the most westerly of the ridges Reynolds had directed the line of battle to be formed and was superintending the placing of Cutler's brigade as he rode up; the ridge is the McPherson Ridge of the gazetteer; the hour is before Reynolds' death at about 10.15 a. m. (next record).

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: General Reynolds had directed his line of battle to be formed,
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 244

place.printed: On the most westerly of these ridges

statement: Doubleday states that Reynolds was killed in the beginning of the attack that the Iron Brigade's charge met, about 10.15 a. m., so that the brigade's charge into the run fell at about that hour.
reasoning: Doubleday prints that Reynolds was shot just after the Iron Brigade's charge and reform, 'in the beginning of the attack referred to', about 10.15 a. m.; the attack referred to is the enemy attack on the wood that the charge met, so the beginning of the Iron Brigade's engagement is dated by the hour of Reynolds' fall.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: in the beginning of the attack referred to, about 10.15 a. m.

statement: Doubleday states that he deemed the extremity of the woods, which extended to the summit of the ridge, to be the key of the position and urged that portion of Meredith's brigade, the Western men assigned to its defense, to hold it to the last extremity.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: to be the key of the iwsition, and urged that portion of Meredith's brigade,

statement: Doubleday states that the principal effort of the enemy was made on the Cashtown road from the northwest and was opposed at first by Cutler's brigade and Hall's battery.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: opposed at first by Cutler's brigade and Hall's battery,

statement: Doubleday states that the Sixth Wisconsin, together with the brigade guard under Lieutenants Harris of the Sixth Wisconsin and Showalter of the Second Wisconsin, had been detached by his order to remain with him as a reserve.
reasoning: Doubleday prints that the Sixth Wisconsin and the brigade guard were detached by his order to remain with him as a reserve; Doubleday took his position behind the left wing (the Iron Brigade's line) and Dawes (R035) puts the regiment's left on the Fairfield road, which Gardner (PA2-S031) calls the Hagerstown road: the nearest gazetteer place is that road near the seminary.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: The Sixth Wisconsin, together with the brigade guard,
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 245

place.printed: to remain with me as a reserve

note: Dawes (R035) prints the same detachment, by command of Doubleday, with the regiment's left on the Fairfield road (record of 1 July). The Fairfield road is the open question of the concordance RC-08; this record names only the Hagerstown road of the gazetteer as the nearest place.

statement: Doubleday states that the brigade guard of the Iron Brigade, under Lieutenants Harris of the Sixth Wisconsin and Showalter of the Second Wisconsin, was detached by his order with the Sixth Wisconsin to remain with him as a reserve.
reasoning: The brigade guard is part of the Iron Brigade (Dawes R035 prints it as the brigade guard); Doubleday prints that it was detached with the Sixth Wisconsin by his order to remain with him as a reserve.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: together with the brigade guard, under Lieutenants Harris,

place.printed: to remain with me as a reserve

statement: Doubleday states that the charge on the railroad cut, the capture of two regiments of Davis' brigade, the release of the 147th New York and the recapture of one of Hall's pieces were all accomplished in less than half an hour and before General Howard had arrived on the field or assumed command.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: All this was accomplished in less than half an hour,
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 246

when.printed: in less than half an hour

place.printed: the railroad cut

statement: Doubleday states that after the railroad cut was carried he immediately directed the original line of battle to be resumed, which was done.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: I immediately directed the original line of battle to be resumed,
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 246

when.printed: I immediately directed the original line of battle to be resumed

place.printed: the original line of battle

note: Doubleday (R029) prints the most westerly of the ridges west of the seminary, about 400 yards west of it, as the ground of the line of battle; Wainwright (R071) and Hall (R072) call it the second ridge; the gazetteer names it McPherson Ridge (GZ-001).

statement: Doubleday states that Tidball's horse battery was ordered up by General Wadsworth to replace Hall's battery, which had been very much cut up, and that soon after Captain Reynolds was sent to relieve him.
reasoning: Doubleday prints that Tidball's horse battery was ordered up by Wadsworth to replace Hall's battery and that soon after Captain Reynolds (Battery L) was sent to relieve him; the ground is the position just vacated by Hall's battery on the right of the Cashtown road near the seminary (Hunt R028 prints Calef 'on the spot just occupied by Hall's').

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: Soon after, Captain Reynolds was sent to relieve him.
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 246

place.printed: to replace Hall's battery

note: Wainwright (R071) and Hunt (R028) print that Wainwright ordered Reynolds with his battery to the support of Calef's battery, placed by Wadsworth on the spot Hall had occupied; Doubleday prints relieve: the two wordings are carried.

statement: Doubleday states that when Robinson's and Rowley's divisions came up he sent Stone's brigade to the open space on the right of the wood to close the interval between Cutler and Meredith, so that the First Division's brigades stood Cutler on the right and Meredith on the left with Stone's brigade between them.
reasoning: Doubleday prints that after Robinson's and Rowley's divisions came up he sent Stone's brigade to the open space on the right of the wood to close the interval between Cutler and Meredith; the interval lay between the two brigades of Wadsworth's division, Cutler's on the right and Meredith's on the left (Doubleday's own order of the Iron Brigade in the wood on the left).

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: to close the interval between Cutler and Meredith.
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 247

when.printed: Just previous to this, the remainder of the First Corps

note: Stone's brigade is a unit of another group; the order recorded here is of the two brigades of this division only.

statement: Doubleday states that when Ewell's corps came from the northeast he changed front, with Wadsworth's division on Stone's brigade as a pivot, so that the two branches of his line of battle faced, the one west, the other northwest; the Iron Brigade on the left of the pivot is read as the branch facing west.
reasoning: Doubleday prints that after Howard formed his lines against Ewell he changed front with Wadsworth's division on Stone's brigade as a pivot so that the two branches of his line faced, the one west, the other northwest; the branch on the left of the pivot was the Iron Brigade in the wood, which held its front toward the west (Maine at Gettysburg, ME-S004, prints Wadsworth's division first formed facing west), and the branch on the right was Cutler's, thrown back to Seminary Ridge to face northwest (Wadsworth R032).

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: were facing, the one west, the other northwest.
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 248

when.printed: General Howard now formed his lines to resist the advance of Ewell

place.printed: Wadsworth's division on Stone's brigade as a pivot

note: The reading of which branch is which is this record's inference (reasoning); the printed words give two bearings. The hour is bounded by Howard's forming against Ewell (about 1 p. m. and after) and Cutler's report that at 2 o'clock a brigade of the Second Division formed on his right (R037).

statement: Doubleday states that after the change of front the two branches of his line of battle faced, the one west, the other northwest; Cutler's brigade, thrown back to Seminary Ridge on the right of the pivot, is read as the branch facing northwest.
reasoning: See the record of the Iron Brigade: the branch on the right of the pivot, which Wadsworth threw back to Seminary Ridge, is read as the branch facing northwest; Wadsworth prints the right line 'northwesterly and diagonal to the Cashtown road' (R032).

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: were facing, the one west, the other northwest.
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 248

when.printed: General Howard now formed his lines to resist the advance of Ewell

place.printed: Seminary Ridge

note: The passage also prints that Wadsworth threw Cutler's brigade back to Seminary Ridge to avoid a battery upon his flank (next record).

statement: Wadsworth states that the enemy advanced in heavy force on his right and placed a battery in position to enfilade the line, and that he was obliged to order the right to fall back to Seminary Ridge, forming the line northwesterly and diagonal to the Cashtown road.

source.author: Brig. Gen. James S. Wadsworth
source.quote: forming the line northwesterly and diagonal to the Cashtown road.
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R032 Brig. Gen. James S. Wadsworth, p. 266

when.printed: The enemy advanced in heavy force on our right

place.printed: Seminary Ridge

note: The word northwesterly is not a compass word the contract's facing basis can carry (the checker reads northwest, not northwesterly); the facing is given by Doubleday's record of the same change of front (the other northwest).

statement: Doubleday states that in consequence of Ewell's new line of battle Wadsworth threw back Cutler's brigade to Seminary Ridge, to avoid a battery upon his flank.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: Wadsworth threw back Cutler's brigade to Seminary Ridge,
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 248

when.printed: In consequence of Ewell's new line of battle

note: Cutler (R037) prints the same retirement from the first position to the woods on the next ridge and the brigade's later orders.

statement: Doubleday states that the change of front of Stone's regiments into the Cashtown road left an open space of some 200 yards between the right of Stone and the left of Cutler, and that Cooper's battery fired through the interval while Biddle's brigade changed front to support it.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: Cooper's battery fired through the interval,
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 248

when.printed: As this left an open space

place.printed: an open space of some 200 yards between the right of Stone and the left of Cutler

note: The interval lay on the Cashtown road between Stone's regiments in the road and Cutler's line; Cooper's battery stood south of the road (Wainwright R071, Hunt R028: an oat-field some 350 to 380 yards south of it).

statement: Doubleday states that the batteries had all been brought back from their advanced positions and posted on Seminary Hill, where they greatly assisted the orderly retreat, retarding the enemy by their fire, and that as they retired to the town the last gun was left, the horses being shot down by skirmishers within 50 yards of the road.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: The batteries had all been brought back from their advanced positions

place.printed: Seminary Hill

note: Wainwright (R071) prints that the batteries moved down the Cashtown pike at a walk and broke into a trot when the infantry had left it; Hunt (R028) prints the same.

statement: Doubleday states that Major-General Hancock, placed in command of both corps, directed him to send a force to support a battery on a lower range of hills some 100 yards east of the position, and that he sent the remainder of Wadsworth's division there; orders from Howard to send the troops another way followed and caused some delay and confusion.
reasoning: Doubleday prints that Hancock, newly arrived and in command, directed him to send a force to support a battery established on a lower range of hills to the east of the position and that he sent the remainder of Wadsworth's division there; Hancock (R076) and Howard (R243) print that Wadsworth's division was placed on the eminence across the Baltimore pike, and the Maine volume (ME-S004) identifies the battery as the Fifth Maine on the knoll at the west end of Culp's Hill: the gazetteer's Culp's Hill and Stevens' Knoll.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: I complied with the order, and sent the remainder of Wadsworth's division there.
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 252

to.printed: a lower range of hills, some 100 yards to the east of our position

note: Doubleday's 100 yards is his own estimate of the distance from the cemetery summit; the hills east of the Baltimore pike (East Cemetery Hill, Culp's Hill and its spur) lie farther; Hancock, Howard and the Maine volume put the division on Culp's Hill and the battery on its western knoll.

statement: Doubleday states that the First Corps, about 8,300 men when it entered the battle, was reduced at the close of the engagement to about 2,450.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday
source.quote: It was reduced at the close of the engagement to about 2,450.
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R029 Maj. Gen. Abner Doubleday, p. 251

statement: Wadsworth states that the right of the division, outnumbered and outflanked, after a resolute contest bravely conducted by Brigadier-General Cutler, fell back in good order to Seminary Ridge, near the town, and a portion of the command to a point still nearer the town.

source.author: Brig. Gen. James S. Wadsworth
source.quote: fell back in good order to Seminary Ridge, near the town,

statement: Wainwright states that one brigade of the First Division had meantime reoccupied the wood where the first engagement took place, and that General Wadsworth sent to ask for a battery, but that with no infantry to protect its right flank he did not consider it safe to place a battery there until the Second Division, just arriving, had taken position.
reasoning: Wainwright prints that one brigade of the First Division had reoccupied the wood of the first engagement and that Wadsworth sent to ask for a battery; the wood of the first engagement is the wood in which the Iron Brigade met Archer (Doubleday R029, Morrow R033).

source.author: Col. Charles S. Wainwright
source.quote: had meantime reoccupied the wood where the first engagement took place,

statement: Wainwright states that when the enemy's first line was within about 200 yards he withdrew Lieutenant Breck's sections of Battery L and ordered them behind a strong stone wall on the seminary crest.

source.author: Col. Charles S. Wainwright
source.quote: ordered him behind a strong stone wall on the seminary crest.
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R071 Col. Charles S. Wainwright, p. 356

when.printed: when their first line was within about 200 yards

place.printed: a strong stone wall on the seminary crest

statement: Wainwright states that an order was now received by Captain Stevens from General Wadsworth to withdraw his battery, but that, not knowing it and under the false impression as to the importance attached to holding Seminary Hill, he directed all the batteries to remain in position until a few minutes later he saw the infantry rapidly retreating to the town.

source.author: Col. Charles S. Wainwright
source.quote: An order was now received by Captain Stevens from General Wadsworth

place.printed: Seminary Hill

statement: Newton states that on 3 July, when the enemy opened with about one hundred and twenty guns near 1 p. m., the batteries of the First Corps, in common with the other batteries in position, vigorously and effectively replied to the enemy's cannonading.
